text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong describes the more than 20 new candidates ruling People's Action Party will field in next election as a strong team and balanced slate.
- Japan must take effective measures to repair damage to Sino-Japanese ties, Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen tells Japanese counterpart in New York.
- Factory worker from China jailed for 16 months for accidental shooting of fiance, a Central Narcotics Bureau officer.
- Conservation and redevelopment sites draw good response in Urban Redevelopment Authority tender.
- Singapore stocks firm on Federal Reserve's decision to leave U.S. interest rates intact.
- Amcol Holdings judicial managers put trading subsidiary Sankei Pte Ltd up for sale because business does not fit in with "White Knight" Sinar Mas's strategy.
- Singapore Press Holdings, Lum Chang Holdings team up to buy Promenade building for Singapore $271 million.
- Rentals for private residential properties slip in second quarter for first time in more than a year.
- Sound card maker Creative Technology shares soar on rumours of a takeover, later denied.
- Regional stock markets end mixed after Wall Street's vacillating reaction to Fed decision not to raise interest rates.
- Talk intensifies of an imminent takeover of PT Astra International, Indonesia's biggest vehicle manufacturer, by tycoon Putera Sampoerna.
- Shangri-La group interim profit up 20 percent to S$9.4 million.
- Hongkong Land net income from properties rises 6.6 percent to US$247.2 million in first half.
- Hai Sun Hup to nearly treble its managed hotels from eight to 22.
